scope: Proposition 5.4 (Uniform insertion probabilities) of the manuscript “Quantum Depletion and Momentum Distribution in the Dilute Hard-Sphere Bose Gas” (preprints/Quantum-Depletion-and-Momentum-Distribution-in-the-Dilute-Hard-Sphere-Bose-Gas-October-5-2026/Quantum-Depletion-in-the-Dilute-Hard-Sphere-Bose-Gas.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 267 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9e8a9907a3ac0811), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 38. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix good data in all neighborhoods met by the following trials. In the first three assertions existing unexposed paths may take any values satisfying their individual cutoffs, while the frozen paths remain those of the fixed data. The fourth assertion instead concerns an obstacle collection satisfying the full-path bounds. For all sufficiently large D, these assertions hold also when an arbitrary subset of avoidance checks is omitted. 1. An ordinary trial Bi, required to satisfy its own cutoffs and avoid the frozen paths and all indicated other unexposed paths, succeeds with probability at least 3/4. 2. A trial formed by choosing a uniform midpoint in a unit cell contained in B(mi, 8b) and at an absolute constant distance from its mean, then choosing independent bridge legs, has success probability at least 3/4. It may also be required to have midpoint distance greater than s from every opponent. 3. Two such trials in two copies, using a common unit cell meeting the preceding conditions for both labels, with a common uniform midpoint and independent legs conditional on that midpoint, simultaneously succeed with probability at least 1/2. Each is checked against the previously present paths in its own copy; the pair is not checked against itself across the copies. 4. Suppose the entire obstacle collection satisfies the motion and count bounds defining the full-path event. A trial pinned at any point within 8b of its mean and more than s from every obstacle midpoint succeeds with probability at least 3/4. This remains valid after adding or substituting a fixed number of individually allowed obstacles, provided the indicated endpoint and midpoint separations hold.
